messages:
ana_support: Escalation from Acme Payments — they report the model is confidently asserting wrong internal details (invented support emails and a non-existent compliance code). Started after yesterday's rollout. Customer is fairly upset. :rotating_light:

emma_cs: Can you paste a minimal repro + the customer-visible response?

ana_support: Pasting the customer's repro (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-l2-13b","prompt":"What is Acme Payments' merchant support email and compliance code?","max_tokens":80}'
```
Response (customer):
```json
{
  "id":"resp_98765f",
  "model":"redwood-l2-13b@2025-01-10",
  "output":"Our merchant support email is support-acme@payments-pro.com and compliance code 77 applies."
}
```
Customer says both pieces are fabricated; the previous model (v2.0 pinned last month) returned: "Please contact support@acmepayments.com; there is no public compliance code."

emma_cs: Thanks. Do they have request_id headers or any server logs from our side?

ana_support: They supplied our request-id header: `req_20250415_98765f`. Also included timestamps and a short list of similar prompts that reproduce the pattern consistently.

raj_eng: Noted. Any recent infra/serving changes for redwood-l2-13b?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: feature "assertion-normalizer-v2" enabled for redwood-l2-13b at 20% traffic at 1959989000.

sofia_research: That feature changed post-processing heuristics to bias towards assertive completions (tries to normalize ambiguous outputs into a concrete claim). Could explain confident fabrications. We also rolled a quantization micro-tweak last week (int8-fastpath) but that usually affects tokenization probabilities, not deterministic assertions. :thinking_face:

liam_prod: Severity escalate — customer revenue impact. Recommend immediate mitigation: pin their tenant to the previous model snapshot and rollback the canary for assertion-normalizer-v2.

raj_eng: Agreed. Triage checklist for eng: 1) Gather model_version & logits for the provided request_id. 2) Re-run customer prompts in our eval harness against both snapshots (pre-rollout and current). 3) If reproduction confirmed, rollback canary to 0% and cut a patch to disable assertion-normalizer for now.

emma_cs: Ana, can you send the customer's prompt set and permission to run it internally? Also ask if they can accept being pinned to the older snapshot while we investigate.

ana_support: On it — customer ok with pinning for now. Sent prompt set to eng + research via a shared S3 link (redacted). They also gave two more request_ids: `req_20250415_98766a` and `req_20250415_98767b`.

sofia_research: I'll run the prompt set through our evaluation harness and dump top-k token probs and the decoding traces. If assertion-normalizer is the cause, we should see post-processing edits that flip low-confidence spans into high-confidence claims.

raj_eng: I'll pull the traces for the provided request_ids now and check kernel/runtime differences (kv-cache behavior, quant path). If we can reproduce locally we can test a rollback.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by raj_eng: canary "assertion-normalizer-v2" -> 0% for redwood-l2-13b at 1959991200. Completion event at 1959991212.

liam_prod: Good. Next steps: notify the customer that we've rolled the canary back and ask them to confirm whether the hallucinations stop after being pinned. Also keep SRE on watch for latency or error spikes from rollback.

ana_support: Notified Acme — they acknowledged and will re-test within the hour. I'll file an official escalation ticket with all details (request_ids, repro set, status). :thumbsup:

sofia_research: If customer reproduces on the older snapshot, that's an indicator of data contamination or prompt sensitivity — we'll dig into training artifacts. If it only reproduces on the canary, it's likely a post-process/regression. Either way, I'll add this prompt set to our regression suite and create an alert for similar assertion changes across customers.

emma_cs: Thanks team. Please tag me on the escalation ticket for customer comms.

ana_support: Will do. Closing the loop here once customer verifies.
